summary: Middlesex County, MA: iron fire tower on Hart's Hill, first operated 1913, closed 1964 and dismantled 1968; register and postcard differ on height and who built it.

facts.design: 48-foot iron tower with spiral stairs and a 10'x10' cab (register); about 50 feet tall (postcard)
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1968; no source describes what remains on the site today

events.note: First operated in 1913 on town park land; postcard credits the state Forestry Department with building it
Closed at the end of the fire season

evidence.supports: design: 48-foot iron tower, spiral stairs, 10x10 cab; built on town park land; first operated 1913
evidence.quote: The 48' iron tower with spiral stairs and a 10'x10' cab was built on town park land and first operated in 1913.

evidence.supports: town of Wakefield contributed $350 toward cost
evidence.quote: The town of Wakefield contributed $350 to the costs of this tower.
In 1958, a new cab was built.

evidence.supports: closed at end of fire season 1964
evidence.quote: In 1964, the tower closed at the end of the fire season.

evidence.supports: dismantled 1968; tower has not stood since
postcard: built at summit in 1913 by the state Forestry Department
evidence.quote: Postcard shows the Hart's Hill forest fire watch tower built at the summit of Hart's Hill in 1913 by the state Forestry Department.
The tower was approximately 50 feet tall.

evidence.supports: register is for a former site; no description of its current state

sources.title: Wakefield Harts Hill Tower Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register (Forest Fire Lookout Association)

notes_for_editor: Read: the FFLOS register page and the Lucius Beebe Memorial Library postcard record (item 17333). Conflicts left open: height 48 ft (register) vs about 50 ft (postcard); the register gives town park land and a $350 town contribution, the postcard says the state Forestry Department built it. Both may hold; no source explains the split. An FFLA Massachusetts Facebook post (search snippet only, login-walled, not opened) reportedly says the tower was steel and used through the end of the 1968 season; that contradicts the register's 1964 closure and 'iron', so it is not used. Do not confuse with Harts Hill in Round Park, Dover, Ohio (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/harts-hill.html), which came up in search. No source read describes the site today. Record 'kind: unknown' could read 'tower' per the register; not changed, no correction proposed.
